sentences.text: Signed by: SUSHEEL KUMAR JHARIYA Signing time: 1/12/2024 5:26:10 PM
2  ORDER

The present petition has been filed seeking the following reliefs:
"(i) A writ in the nature of mandamus be issued to comman the respondents to produce entire record pertaining to Case No.439/B- 121/2023-24 parties being Laxminarayan Chakravarty vs. State of M.P. and others, Mouza Medholi from the respondent No.3 - Collector, Singrauli (M.P.) for kind perusal and ready reference of this Hon'ble Court.

entities.text: Laxminarayan Chakravarty vs. State of M.P. and others, Mouza Medholi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(ii) That, this Hon'ble Court may further be pleased to issue a writ in the nature of certiorari to set aside impugned order dated 30.06.2023 passed by respondent no.3 contained in Annexure P/6 and further be pleased to allow Claim-cum-objection filed by the petitioner contained in Annexure P/2 keeping in view documents contained in Annexure P/3 and P/4 which are the Patwari Report and the same have been produced in light of order dated 20.12.2017 passed by the respondent no.2 and conveniently ignored by the respondent no.2, in the interest of justice.
(iii) Any other writ, order or direction, which this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case, may also kindly be passed, in the interest of justice."

2. It is the case of the petitioner that land bearing Khasra No.354/4/13 area 0.008 hectare situated at village Medholi, Tehsil & District Singrauli has been acquired by the respondents and an award to the aforesaid effect has been passed on 20.12.2013 to the tune of Rs.9,49,762/-.
It is his case that a very less compensation has been awarded by the authorities.

He has filed a claim-cum- objection under Section 3(G)(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 before the prescribed authority but the authority has not considered the case of the petitioner and dismissed the same.
The same was put to challenge before the respondent no.2 - Commissioner, Rewa Division Rewa, who has asked the respondent no.3 to consider the claim of the petitioner and pass a final order.

The respondent no.3 passed the impugned order on the ground that neither any document is being placed by the petitioner on record in support of the arguments not does he want to file any documentary evidence.

Therefore, the Collector has arrived at a conclusion that there is no infirmity in the award and dismissed the same vide order dated 30.06.2023, which is order impugned in this petition.
3.

Counsel appearing for the petitioner when confronted with the fact that he himself has denied for filing any documentary evidence before the Collector, he submits that he was not in possession of the documents on that date.
Now he has procured the documents and filed along with this petition.

Therefore, instead of getting an order on merits, a prayer is made that the matter be remanded back to the Collector i.e. the respondent no.3 for reconsideration of the case of the petitioner considering the documents which are being filed by him in the present petition.

sentences.text: 4. Counsel for the respondents has no objection to the innocuous prayer made by the petitioner, but he submits that the Collector may be free to pass an appropriate order in accordance with law after taking into consideration the documents filed by the petitioner.

5. Looking to the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case and the fact that the claim of the petitioner is yet to be considered on merits by the authorities and to substantiate the arguments that he has certain documents which were not filed before the Collector on earlier occasions and that the petitioner being a villager is having no understanding of nicety of law and the fact that he should not be made sufferer for the same, this Court deems it appropriate to set aside the order passed by the Collector and remand the matter back to him with a liberty to the petitioner to place on record all the documents which he wants to place reliance upon before the Collector.
6. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
The impugned order dated 30.06.2023 passed by the Collector is set aside.
The matter is remanded back to the Collector to consider and decide the case of the petitioner afresh after taking note of the documents which will be filed by the petitioner.
The petitioner is at liberty to place all the documents before the Collector in support of his claim.

The petitioner to appear before the Collector along with all the documents on or before 22.01.2024.
7.
The entire exercise be completed within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.
8. With the aforesaid, the petition stands allowed and disposed off.
No order as to costs.
(RAVI MALIMATH) (V  CHIEF JUSTICE   sj Laxmi Narayan Chakravarty vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50814434/
